summary: Prefetch threshold oscillation in continuous batcher causing intermittent p95/p99 latency waves for streaming requests
description: Issue summary: Since 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC, TileWave Labs has reported intermittent p95/p99 latency waves (streaming responses timing out or stalling) on their dedicated deployment. The pattern is periodic: 10-20 minute low-latency periods followed by sudden 2-8 minute windows of elevated tail latency for short streaming requests. Impact: Customer-facing features time out for end users (~3% of requests during peaks), causing degraded UX and ticketed escalations. Environment: Dedicated pool in us-east-1 serving redwood/gptx-13b-8bit with continuous-batcher enabled and prefetch threshold tuned to 32 tokens. Observed start: 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC. Current status: In Progress — SRE and runtime eng investigating.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a sustained stream of short generation requests (1-20 tokens) to TileWave's dedicated endpoint in prod-us-east at ~25 QPS from multiple client IPs. 2) Ensure continuous-batcher mode is enabled with prefetch_threshold=32 and idle_linger_ms=12. 3) Observe p95/p99 latency over a 30 minute window; the issue typically reproduces after 8-12 minutes of traffic fluctuations. Note: reproduction is non-deterministic and appears correlated with small bursts from multiple tenants in the same pool.
observed_metrics: - p50 stable ~80ms, p95 spikes from ~180ms to 850ms, p99 spikes up to 2200ms. - Increase in streaming reconnects and 504s during peaks (customer reports timeouts). - batcher_coalesce_delay metric shows periodic jumps from 6ms to 180ms correlating with latency waves.
hypothesis: Prefetch threshold interacts with tenant-aware reweighting and an idle-linger hysteresis in the continuous batcher; when a tenant's burst pattern crosses the prefetch threshold boundary the batcher flips between aggressive prefetching and conservative flush behavior, creating resonant accumulation and delayed flushes (head-of-line effects). This produces periodic micro-batch backlog and long-tail latency for short streaming requests.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 03:00 UTC — Support acknowledged and requested telemetry from customer (request-id examples).
2026-03-12 05:10 UTC — SRE collected Datadog flamegraphs; saw sampler threads paused when batcher_coalesce_delay jumps.
2026-03-12 08:22 UTC — Runtime team reproduced locally with synthetic traffic using same prefetch_threshold and observed same sawtooth p99 pattern.

2026-03-13 11:40 UTC — Confirmed tenant-reweighting events coincide with jitter in batching timers (related to PR that adjusted tenant weight recalculation frequency). See linked PR for weight recalculation: https://github.com/redwood/realtime-batcher/pull/285
2026-03-14 09:15 UTC — Test toggling prefetch_threshold to 16 reduced amplitude of p99 spikes in staging; setting to 8 eliminated spikes but increased total token cost by ~6% during test window.
2026-03-14 11:00 UTC — Identified a race where prefetch counter and idle_linger_ms update path do not acquire same locks leading to transient misread of effective threshold under load.
Next steps — preparing a targeted patch to synchronize threshold updates and add smoothing to tenant weight changes; plan to deploy canary to a subset of dedicated pools.
resolution: Mitigation in progress. Temporary workaround provided: recommend lowering prefetch_threshold to 8 for affected TileWave clusters (config change applied to their dedicated pool) and enabling short-lived increased batch flush frequency via scheduler toggle. This reduced p99 peaks to within SLA during validation. Permanent fix: runtime patch to atomically update prefetch counters with tenant weight changes and add low-pass filter to prefetch behavior. Rollout scheduled as canary on 2026-03-16.
